hypothesis: Object permanence requires consulting retained identities before committing a new identity, including high-score reappearances. Weak-only recovery with at most8-frame point evidence misses most long-gap identity discontinuities.
setting: Keep the actual November DiffV2IR input and fixed matched detector frontends. The frozen fitted RGB reference plus its matched extra-RGB or IR residual scores identity evidence; no new data generation or detector adaptation.
current_observation: Only real current detector observations with score>=0.3; retained IDs are eligible only if emitted in a strictly earlier frame. Existing identities already emitted earlier may never be reassigned. A newly created or newly confirmed ID may be suppressed only before its first output is returned.
memory: Retain actual past observation indices and objects. Compare ordinary25-frame retention with an explicit128-frame archive, and latest-observation with a past-only clear-observation anchor. Never read a later feature row or rewrite earlier outputs.
clear_anchor: Update the clear anchor only when the actual current object box has IoU<=0.3 with every other current score>0.6 proposal and its RGB contrast>=0.15. The rule is identical for both cue controls. Otherwise keep the previous clear observation, falling back to the latest actual observation if none exists.
appearance_only: When point transport is unavailable or when an old anchor is outside lags1/2/4/8, use the exact registered Train-long-bank feature masking: absent ownership votes and point survival are zero, unknown spatial IoU/centre displacement and motion-quality channels are zero, retained RGB/cue descriptors and contrast are real past/current values, lag feature is capped at8. Do not fabricate motion evidence.
competition: Score an old identity against every current candidate, including observations owned by active identities. Require its best current observation to remain eligible, raw RGB cosine>=0.5, calibrated probability>=0.9, and a0.1 margin over all other current observations and competing retained identities. Use one-to-one assignment and abstain on ties. An ambiguous appearance match does not justify old-ID reuse.
motion_reset: On an accepted semantic recovery initialize the Kalman state at the actual current observation before reactivation with the old ID; a stale long-gap predicted location must not distort the returned box.
archive_bound: Expire references128 frames after their most recent actual observation; at most the identities actually emitted in this bounded interval. No full image memory or dataset copies.
planned_Dev_pairs: No prebirth recovery with exact fitted-reference inheritance
Latest-observation prebirth recovery with original25-frame retention
Latest-observation prebirth recovery with explicit128-frame archive
Clear-observation prebirth recovery with explicit128-frame archive
Conservative0.95 probability with explicit128-frame archive and clear anchor
controls: All three seeds and both identically trained cue heads. A same-code extra-RGB control is mandatory. Generic archive, Kalman reset and RGB descriptors alone receive no multimodal innovation credit.
selection: Fix all candidate configurations before accuracy. Select checkpoints only by complete Dev under each learned family's registered common stopping rule; preserve all failures. Test cannot select retention, probability, anchor or model weights.
required_tests: A never-emitted fresh ID may be replaced by an eligible old ID using only the current real observation
A previously emitted identity is immutable even when another archived ID scores higher
No ambiguous old-ID reuse; one observation cannot reactivate two IDs
Retained old-ID recovery beyond25 frames only when the explicit archive is enabled
Disabled recovery reproduces the exact parent outputs and lifecycle
Future descriptors cannot change any emitted prefix
goal: At least+5 complete-Test HOTA over direct RGB fine-tune29.529 and2-3 independently supported modality-specific contributions; not established by this registration.
